      CHAPTER – I 
  
  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
  
  
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
          Last but not the least, under the present scen ario of stiff competition from private and global companies, th e
DPE should strengthen the MoU system specially where is sues involving inter-ministerial/ inter PSU co-ordinatio n
are concerned. The DPE should play a pro-active role in making the PSUs competitive and strengthening them fo r
sustained growth. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
            Efforts are made during the MOU negotiat ion meetings to achieve the inter-ministerial and inter-PSU 
coordination. The incorporation of PSU-s pecific efficiency parameters in the MOUs is an attempt to improve the 
profitability and competitive strength of the PSUs. Theref ore, the MOU system already plays, an active role in 
strengthening the PSEs to become more competitive. These efforts will be further continued.  
  
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
The MoU system has undeniably made a positive contribu tion to improve the performance of the PSEs.  The 
management of PSEs were appreciative of the fact that the MoU system has, for the first time brought about clarity o f 
the goals to be achieved on the basis of precise targets laid down in the MoU ensuring accountability on an objective 
basis.  They were also enthusiastic of the larger delegati on of powers available to the MoU signing Companies.  The 
managements of the PSEs could act freely to a great extent with clear-cut objec tives and goals.  Especially in thei r 
day-to-day operations, the interference by the Ministries had reduced to a considerable extent. This has provided an 
opportunity to the managements to take quick decisions and furthermore, evaluation of their performance is now 
being done in a very objective and transparent basis. 
  
  
COMMENTS 
  
The observations of the Standing Committee on the work ing of the MOU system are taken note of and efforts 
will be made to further strengthen it.  
  
   
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
The Committee also feels that through the MoU system, an effort has been made to synthesise different 
objectives.  Under the MoU system the parameters selected  as performance indicators ar e a good mix of financial, 
dynamic and efficiency indicators.  Thus, it is not only the financial parameters  which are given importance but other 
dynamic and efficiency parameters  whic h are very essential for the future growth of the PSEs, and which are also 
incorporated as performance indicators.  Thus, under the present system an attemp t has been made to strike a balance 
between financial and non-financial parameters.  The Comm ittee is of the firm view that the MoU system has 
produced reasonable results as it is unders tood that during the negotiation meetings an effort is made to set targets, 
which represent an improvement over the level of performance  in the previous year, and the system has significantly 
contributed to a progressive increase in the performance of PSEs.  The Committee, ther efore, recommends that the 
MoU system should continue on a long-term basis. 
  
COMMENTS

            The observations of the Standing Committee on the importance of MOU system has been taken note of and it 
has been decided to continue the system on a long term basis.         
   
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
Recently, the Public Sector Enterprises have been expos ed to domestic and international competition.  Most 
of them were operating in a totally protective environmen t.  With the policy of liberalisation and globalisation, the 
PSEs have to compete in the market for obtaining orders bot h in products and services.  For a PSE to be competitive 
it is essential to have an edge over its competitors, both in cost and quality.  In such a situation, the Committee feels 
that  up gradation of technology including modernisation, up gradation of skills of em ployees and rationalisation o f 
manpower etc. are key factors to generate necessary comp etitive strength to PSEs.  The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the MoU system should be used as an effective instrument to bring about the change in the working 
environment of the PSEs by introducing specific strategies through it to make them more competitive. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
            To a large extent technology upgradati on, modernisation, upgradation of skills of employees and 
rationalisation of manpower etc. generally form part of the dynamic parameters, which are incorporated in the MOUs. 
However, more emphasis will be laid on these issues while  issuing the guidelines for formulation of draft MOUs fo r 
next year.  
  
   
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
On the question of reduction of budgetary support to Depa rtment of Public Enterprises and its consequent 
winding up in pursuance of recommendation of Expenditure  Reforms Commission (EFC), it has not considered the 
essentially vital role played by the  Department of P ublic Enterprises in making the Memoranda of Understanding 
which the Government of India enters with its Public Sector  Units on the annual basis.  The Department is merely not 
facilitating but enabling the MoU to be an important tool for performance assessment mutates mutandis to that o f 
Profit Center Concepts of large Conglomerates in devel oped countries.  The MoU is an  effective and objective tool 
today only because of it being facilitate d by a non-stakeholder that is Department  of Public Enterprises.  Hence, the 
Committee strongly feels that the Department of  Public Enterprises should be strengthened with budgetary support.   
  
COMMENTS 
  
The   objective of MOU system was to improve the performance of PSEs  and to intruduce a mechanism to 
evaluate the performance of the managements in an objective and transparent manner and it was in this interest, the 
job of implementing the MOU system was entrusted to a nodal Department. The need to strengthen the Department 
with budgetary support is taken note of and will be reviewed while formulating the budget proposals. 
  
   
RECOMMENDATION 
  
The Committee observes that the strength of the MoU system is that the targets are finalised and the 
performance of the PSE is evaluated in an objective and transparent manner that is ensured by the DPE and ATF.  
Thus, in order to maintain and further instil objectivity, th e Committee feels that DPE should play a more active role 
in the process and the MoU Division should be strengthene d so that they can carry out bench marking studies, 
performance related studies and other associated work so that the targets given to the PSEs are more realistic. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
               The MOU Division has the benefit of getting the advice of the ATF which is a body of experts an d
academicians eminent in their respective fields. Functi ons like conduction benchmark studies, performance relate d
studies can be sourced out to prominent professional bodi es. The need for strengthening MOU Division and playing a
more active role in the process has been take note of.

RECOMMENDATION 
  
             The Committee is, however, constrained to note that the MoU Division of the Department of  Public 
Enterprises has been proposed to be abolished.  The Secret ary, Ministry of Heavy Indus try and Public Enterprises, 
during the course of his oral evidence before the Committee in connection with the Demands for Grants, informed the 
Committee that the Expenditure Reforms Commission has recommended that the Department of Public Enterprises 
may be down-sized .  It was proposed that  the  MoU Syst em  may be transferred to the respective Administrative
Ministries of the concerned PSEs. The Committee, however, does not agree with this.   The Committee feels that the 
Department of Public Enterprises provides a neutral forum for finalising MoUs  which is essential to make it an 
objective systems.  It is also ensured that the entire MoU ex ercise is carried out in an objective, transparent and broad 
based manner.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that instead of transferring the MoU System to the concerned 
Administrative Departments, it may be retained with the De partment of Public Enterprise s. In fact the MoU Division 
needs to be further strengthened for an effective implementation of the MoU System.  
  
COMMENTS 
  
In order to ensure the objectivity of the system the job of implementing the MOU system was entrusted to a 
nodal Department, if the task of  preparing/finalising the MOUs is left to the respective concerned Administrative 
Ministries such a situation is bound to defeat the very purpose of having the MOU system. It has accordingly been 
decided not to transfer the MOU related work to the Admini strative Ministries and it will continue to the with DPE 
whose nodal and neutral status will be maintained. As regards the need for strengthening the MOU Division the 
recommendation of the Committee has been noted.  
  
CHAPTER-II 
  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATION WHICH THE COMMITTEE  
 DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENTS’ REPLIES  
  
  
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
The Committee is constrained to note that the MoU prep aration has generally been an annual target setting 
exercise.  The Committee feels that the MoU system should focus on strategic issues rather than be a mere annual 
target setting exercise.  For that purpose the Administ rative Ministries should provi de adequate input/support to 
enable PSEs to develop future strategies in association wi th the Ministries.  The parameters under the MoU need to 
be devised depending upon the strategy for its future growth in the particular area of its operations.  The performance 
of the PSEs needs to be reviewed on the basis of parameters so devised.  This would give a clear picture as to how a 
particular PSE has been able to make its products/services  cost effective and how they compare with their counte r 
parts in the private sector.  Such an approach would certa inly make the PSEs not only competitive but also provide an 
opportunity to become global players.  Therefore, the Committee suggests that the approach under the MoU system 
needs to be reviewed in line with the existing competitive economic environment. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
The Ad-hoc Task Force is already seized of this issue and during the MOU ne gotiation meetings, great 
importance is attached to the strategic issues. Further efforts in this regard will continue to bring to the notice of the 
PSEs and Administrative Ministries, the crucial importance of the strategi c issues and impressing upon them to 
develop appropriate strategies for improvement of the performance of the PSEs.  
  
   
RECOMMENDATION

It is felt that setting  up of an Export Promotion Cell for CPSUs in DPE may cut across the legitimate

the front end, it can invite, in the fi rst instance, other concerned telecom PSUs to be consortium partners, on the basis

            The Committee desires that the DPE should c ontinuously review the progress made in this regard and monito r

RECOMMENDATION 
  
There have been persistent efforts by various Depart ments with the Finance Ministry to correct the duty 
structure.  With the liberalisation, the duties on the finished goods have come down faster than the duties on the raw 
materials in electronic and information technology.  If the duty structure is not corrected , the people will find import

            The Committee is of the view that rationa lisation of the duty structure is  of utmost importance to mak e

RECOMMENDATION 
  
Though the parameters such as preparation and implem entation of corporate plan  and devising a strategic 
plan or vision plan, etc. are being me ntioned in the MoU documents, the targets set in the MoUs do not often 
correspond to the corporate vision/plans drawn up by the PSEs.  The Committee, therefore, stresses that there should 
be a better linkage between the corporate plans of the PSEs and the MoUs.  
  
COMMENTS 
  
            Most of the PSEs have now formulated co rporate plans, as this has been impressed upon them during the 
MOU negotiation meetings. This recommendation of  the Standing Committee has been noted and the 
PSEs/Administrative Ministries  will be requested through the guidelines that are proposed to be issued for the 
formulation of MOUs for the next year to try and establish the necessary linkages between the corporate plans and the 
MOU targets.  
  
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATIONS  
  
            DPE  may ensure implementation of this by a ll Ministries. This is necessary because if the targets of MOUs 
do not correspond with corporate vision/plans, the MOUs preparation  will be a futile exercise.   
  
   
RECOMMENDATION 
  
As PSEs have to operate in a free market, they cannot continue to depend upon Government’s assistance on 
matters such as obtaining orders, etc.  In the present situ ation, negotiating for orders is  a managerial function and, 
therefore, the Government’s  intervention should be very sel ective, if at all.  For inst ance, a number of the PSEs are 
working in the same area but they are under the control of different administrative minist ries.  In some cases, these 
PSEs operate as competitors to each other.  Similarly, PSEs are also involved in research and development projects 
and some of the PSEs are spending quite a significant  MoU units  on R&D activities.  Unfortunately, these PSEs are 
working in isolation and there is no coordination to provide synergy in R& D, marketing, etc. to enhance thei r 
competitive edge over their counter partners in the private sectors.  Since these PSEs are functioning in watertight 
compartments, they are not able to reap the maximum benefits of their investments on R&D and up gradation o f 
technology.  Separate and isolated efforts on the part of the PSEs in such areas only result in addition to their costs.  
Therefore, there is tremendous scope in bringing together  PSEs operating in the same discipline, but under different 
Ministries, to optimise inve stments in marketing, R&D etc. in a collect ive and coordinated manner.  The Committee, 
therefore, feels that the Department of Public Enterp rises operating through the MoU system appears to be an 
appropriate forum where the issues involving inter-ministries /inter-PSEs coordination can be taken up more 
effectively and DPE as a nodal Department should play a mo re pro-active role in making the PSEs competitive and 
strengthening them for sustained growth. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
            The possibility of such synergy exists  particularly in the area of R&D, Technology up gradation and 
marketing. Sub optimal investment by individual PSEs often does not generate  productive results. On the other hand, 
a collaborative effort in the field of R&D and marketing by pooling the resources of different enterprises can produce 
useful results. In the MOU negotiation meetings, it is generally attempted to bring together PSEs in the same 
discipline and explore such possibilities.

REPORT
         The Sixty Second Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the Recommendations contained in its 48th
Report of the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry on the Demands For Grants 2000-2001 pertaining to the
Department of Public Enterprises  which was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on  the 14th  May, 2001.
 
2.         Action Taken Notes have been received from the Government in respect of the recommendations contained in the Report. They have been
categorized as follows:
             
 (i)        Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Government:- Para  6.14;  6.15;  6.16;  6.17;  6.18 and 6.19.   ( Chapter -
I).
 
 (ii)       Recommendation/Observation which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the government’s replies: - Para  2.8;  4.3 and 4.5 .
   (Chapter - II).
 
 (iii)      Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted replies of the Government: - Para 2.5;  3.5;  3.9;  4.5; 
5.4;  5.6;  5.7 and 5.8. (Chapter - III).
 
 (iv)      Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government have not been received: -NIL. (Chapter – IV).
           
  (v)      Observations/Recommendations at a Glance . (Chapter – V).
CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY      THE GOVERNMENT
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
After hearing the Secretary, Department of Public Enterprises, the Committee expressed its unhappiness that the Expenditure Reforms Commission
has recommended that the task of preparing MoUs can be left as well to the concerned administrative Ministries.  The Committee feels that the said
Commission in an anxiety to reduce the Government expenditure undermined the role of a nodal agency, i.e., Department of Public Enterprises
without evaluating its performance over the years.
COMMENTS
 
The recommendations of the Committee were kept in view while reviewing the role and functions of DPE in the context of the recommendations
made by the ERC and it has been decided that the work relating to MOU can not be transferred to the Administrative Ministries and should continue
to be performed by the DPE in the interest of maintaining objectivity and credibility of the system apart from ensuring transparency and
accountability.
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee is also of the view that a unified central agency to implement the MoU system is certainly more cost effective rather than
having separate MoU Units in all the Administrative Ministries.  Similarly, pooling expertise for all the Ministries from the same ATF as is being
done at present by the Department of Public Enterprises is also cost effective.
 
COMMENTS
 
The recommendations of the Committee have been kept in view and it has been decided to continue with the present arrangement of implementing
the MOU System by the nodal Department namely, DPE rather than leaving the task of preparing MOUs to the concerned Administrative Ministries
as recommended by the ERC.  The present system of implementing MoU System through a unified central agency like DPE is not only cost-
effective but also imparts objectivity and credibility to the system.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee further feels that the Department of Public Enterprises provides a neutral forum for finalizing the MoUs, which is essential
to make it an objective system, and it should not be abolished.
 
COMMENTS
 
Government agrees with the view of the Committee that a neutral forum like the Department of Public Enterprises is necessary for finalizing MOUs
to make it an objective system. Government has no intention to dilute its nodal and neutral status as at present.
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee is also of the firm view that the object of signing MoUs would not be achieved in the absence of an over-seeing agency, i.e.
Department of Public Enterprises.
 

62nd Report

COMMENTS
 
The Government agrees with the views of the Committee. DPE’s status as a nodal and neutral over-seeing agency will continue.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the proposal of abolishing MoU Division may be shelved.  As the country is now on
the threshold of making PSEs more vibrant, productive and efficient, it is very essential that the MoU Division should be further strengthened
instead of being abolished.  Strengthening of MoU Division would go a long way in making PSEs profitable and responsive to competitiveness.
 
COMMENTS
 
The Government accepts the recommendations of the Committee. There is no proposal to abolish the MOU Division. As regards strengthening this
Division, position is reviewed from time to time  and appropriate action  taken wherever necessary.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee, therefore, again recommends that the Department of Public Enterprises should be strengthened so as to make it more
responsive.
 
COMMENTS
 
The recommendations of the Committee have been noted. Periodical review of the organizational structure of DPE is being conducted and
whenever necessary, action is being taken to strengthen the Department to make it more responsive.
CHAPTER-II
 
THE COMMITTEE DOES  NOT DESIRE TO PURUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT' S REPLIES
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The committee is of the view that the present staff strength numbering about 136 of the Department of Public Enterprises needs to be
increased in view of the wide roles and functions being undertaken by the Department.  The Department needs to be strengthened.
 
COMMENTS
 
In the context of the recommendations of the Expenditure Reforms Commission (ERC), the role and functions of the Department were reviewed and
15 posts at various levels were abolished. The above recommendation  has been noted and the staff strength will be reviewed as per needs and due
strengthening and rationalisation will be done  where required.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The existing rate of Rs.9000 per head for non-recurring expenses towards infrastructure, office equipments, preparatory works, training
expenses, follow-up services, etc. of nodal agency, may prove insufficient.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the existing rate of Rs.9000
per head may be reviewed.  If necessary,  the allocation may be increased.
 
COMMENTS
 
This is the first year of implementation of  the Training programme  by the Department of Public Enterprises. The advice of the Committee is being
noted and while reviewing  the working of the scheme, the per head cost along with other aspects of the scheme would  be considered.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee feels that the Department of Public Enterprises is over burdened after being assigned the tasks of counselling, retraining and
redeployment of rationalized employees of Central PSEs.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Public Enterprises should
involve/appoint new technocrats, Research Officers, skilled workers etc.
COMMENTS
 
The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. The position with regard to implementation of the scheme would be reviewed periodically,
when the manpower requirement could also be reviewed.
 
                CHAPTER-III
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE  NOT  BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT

62nd Report

RECOMMENDATION
 
            Since substantial new tasks have been assigned to the Department of Public Enterprises, the allocation of Rs.10.86 crores made for the year
2001-2002 does not appear to be sufficient.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the allocation made to the department by the Government
may be reviewed in the supplementary demands for grants.
 
COMMENTS
 
As far as the work relating to retraining and redeployment of rationalized employees of PSEs is concerned, this is the first year of implementation of
the Training Programme by the Department of Public Enterprises. The recommendation of the Committee is being noted and will be kept in view
while reviewing the Scheme.
 
 
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATION
           
The Committee is of the view that the work relating to retraining and redeployment of rationalised employees of central PSEs recently assigned to
the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) is an important matter in the present context, which needs to be reviewed and monitored periodically.
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee, however, would like to know how far such an enlarged Board of Directors consisting of official/non-officials/part time
Directors has produced the desired results.  The Committee feels that the Department of Public Enterprises should undertake a study in the matter.
 
COMMENTS
 
While granting enhanced autonomy and authority under Navratna and Miniratna, one of the preconditions was that Boards of these Navratna and
Miniratna CPSUs should be professionalised by inducting of non-official part-time Directors through Search Committee. Accordingly the exercise
for professionalisation of Boards in case of existing 11 Navratna CPSUs was completed in April, 1999.  In case of Miniratna, Board of Directors of
17 CPSUs out of 46 have been restructured by co-opting part-time professional Directors. It may be mentioned that the Boards are not enlarged, but
only vacant positions have been filled.
A study was carried out in consultation with all the 11 navratna PSUs and those Miniratna PSUs, where non-official part-time Directors have been
inducted. It is revealed that the Boards have exercised the enhanced powers to a large extent. The induction of non-official Directors has helped in
professionalising the Boards of these PSUs and also to set up various sub-committees like Audit Committee. The non-official Directors with their
rich experience and expertise in various areas like management, administration, finance, marketing, technology, etc. have contributed substantially
in the Board deliberations. Thus the study has revealed that the by and large induction of non-official professional Directors has produced the
desired results.
 
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATION
 
            The Committee feels that autonomy of  PSUs should not be limited by Govt. control and such Companies should be fully Board-managed
Companies in all matters. In an environment of stiff competition in the post liberalisation era, the PSUs can not function effectively without
sufficient freedom of operation and level playing field. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Boards of Directors of at least MOU-signing
Companies should be given sufficient powers to enable them to take quick decisions in their business related  matters, by reviewing the extent of the
current powers relating to limit on investment, access to capital market, repayment of foreign loans, foreign visits  by Boards of Directors for their
business position,  forming of joint ventures, exploring foreign markets etc. 
 
            The Committee feels that many PSUs remain headless without any CMD for a long time. This cripples the functioning of the PSUs.
Therefore, as and when any PSU is without CMD for three months, immediate action should be taken to appoint CMD. The Committee understands
that the appointments of CMDs of Central  PSUs is done by Public Enterprises Selection Board. Earlier this Board was under the Department of
Public Enterprises which is presently being controlled by the Ministry of Personnel & Training . The Committee, therefore, recommends that this
Board may be shifted from the purview of  the Ministry of Personnel & Training  to the Department of Public Enterprises for an effective 
monitoring  of  the functioning of the Central PSUs.
 
            Smaller PSUs at micro level are facing lot of challenges of the competition. The best way to make PSUs viable is to merge the related PSUs
so that the competition can be effectively faced. For this Government  may appoint a Committee to look into the issue of merger.
 
            The Committee further observes that only 108 PSUs out of 240 PSUs have signed the MoU system  with their Administrative
Ministries/Departments. The Committee stresses that all profit making PSUs should be brought under the ambit of the MoU system.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee, however, feels that the Department of Public Enterprises should review the performance of such companies in order to
know whether such companies are maintaining the status for which they were awarded such elevated positions.  The Committee feels that the
procedure to accord the Navratna status is a tardy procedure which needs to be revised by the Government.  Secondly, the responsibility of
accordance of the status of Miniratna, presently being held by the respective administrative ministries themselves to the concerned PSE, must be
transferred to the Search Committee under the Department of Public Enterprises.

COMMENTS
 
In May, 2001 the Government  issued guidelines for review of performance of Navratna and Miniratna Enterprises and for divest/grant of Navratna
and Miniratna status as the case may be which covers the points raised by the Committee.  These guidelines include:
 
Apex Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary in the case of Navratna enterprises and Inter-Ministerial Committee headed by the Secretary,
Department of Public Enterprises in the case of Miniratna enterprises would regularly review the performance of such companies.
A comprehensive review would be undertaken every three years by the above mentioned respective Committees with regard to maintenance of the
Navratna/Miniratna status.  The Apex Committee would lay down the format for such a review.
The Apex Committee would also review the operations of Navratna/Miniratna schemes every three years and would make recommendations in
regard to further delegation of autonomy to these enterprises
The recommendations of the Apex Committee, if any, for divestment of the Navratna status would be put up to the Minister(Heavy Industries and
Public Enterprises) for approval through the Minister in-charge of the administrative Ministry concerned.  In case of any disagreement, the matter
would be put up to the cabinet.
The recommendations of the divestment of Miniratna status would be dealt with by concerned administrative Ministry only.
 
The recommendations for accordance of Navratna status to a CPSU would, ordinarily, not be placed before the Cabinet.  Based on the
recommendations of the Apex Committee these would be placed before the Minister for Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises for taking a final
decision.  But as in (iv) above, in case of disagreement, the matter would be put up to the Cabinet.
 
This guideline has set in place separate Committee to review the performance of Navaratna and Miniratna PSEs. The periodicity of the review will
be every 3 years. It has also laid down the procedure for according Navaratna Status.
 
The recommendation of assigning the task of accordance of the status of Miniratnas to the Search Committee under DPE has been noted and will be
kept in view at the time of reviewing of the existing mechanism.
 
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATION
 
            The Committee desires that an early decision may be taken regarding assigning the tasks of accordance of the status of Miniratnas to the
Search Committee under DPE. The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation that the procedure to accord Navaratna status may be revised
and simplified.
RECOMMENDATION  (5.4)
 
            The Committee recommends that the Purchase Preference Policy should be extended for another 3 years, i.e., upto 31.3.2004
 
COMMENTS
 
Recommendation of the Committee has been noted and the position will be reviewed at appropriate time.
           
RECOMMENDATION ( 5.6 )
 
            The Committee is very much concerned to note that certain Central PSEs/Central Govt. Agencies are not including the Purchase Preference
clause in their Notice Inviting Tender(NIT) depriving the other Central PSEs to avail the benefit of the Government Policy.  This non-cooperative
attitude of some of the PSEs does not go well with the overall policy of the government to improve the health of PSEs.  The highlights indicated by
the Minister would remain only highlights without a major shift in their health status.  If there has to be a major reversal in the health condition of
the PSEs, all the PSEs  need to have mutual cooperation.  Purchase Preference Policy is one such grey area which, if followed scrupulously by all
the PSUs, would improve the performance of all the ailing PSEs.
 
COMMENTS
 
Govt. have noted the recommendations of the Committee.
 
RECOMMENDATION  (5.7)
 
            The Committee, therefore, recommends that all the Administrative Ministries/Government Departments should issue the instructions to the
PSEs under their jurisdiction to comply with the policy of the Government on Purchase Preference.
COMMENTS
 
DPE  issues general guidelines on various issues pertaining to CPSUs.  It is for the concerned Administrative Ministry/Department to ensure that the
guidelines issued by the Government including DPE are implemented by the PSUs.  The recommendations of the Committee will be circulated to

RECOMMENDATION  (5.8)
 
The Committee also recommends that the Department of Public Enterprises should ensure and monitor the compliance of the Purchase Preference
Policy.  In this regard all Public Sector Enterprises may be asked to submit documents of NIT to the Department of Public Enterprises for regular

compliance.
 
COMMENTS
 
Government have noted the recommendation of the Committee and would take appropriate action at the time of review of the policy
 
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATIONS ON THE PURCHASE PREFERENCE POLICY ------  ( 5.4,  5.6,  5.7 & 5.8 )
 
(1-5.4)             In this connection, the Sub-Committee-III for the Ministry of Heavy Industries & Public Enterprises took up this matter for
consideration and held discussions with the Secretary, the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises.
 
The Secretary observed that if the PSEs were to be efficient, the crutches were to be removed. The Secretary informed that this policy provided
Purchase Preference in supply of goods and services to the government departments and other PSEs if the price quoted by the supplying PSE was
within 10% of the lowest valid bid price, other things being equal.  The policy was extended up to 31.3.02.  He pointed out that 51 PSUs took
advantage of the policy and 22 PSUs awarded the contracts under the policy.  There had been cases where Purchase Preference clause was not
included in the Notice Inviting Tenders (NIT).  The Administrative Ministries/Departments had been told to ensure that the guidelines issued by the
Government including D/o Public Enterprises were implemented by the PSEs.  He observed that there was slackness in following the guidelines and
it became difficult to correct action at a later stage wherever a violation of the guidelines took place.
 
            The Sub-Committee also held discussions with the CMDs of  many CPSUs and most of them have agreed that this policy should be
extended beyond 31.3.3002 and were also of the view that the policy should be strictly complied with by all PSUs.
 
            The Committee is  of the firm view that in the interest of the Nation and well being of the PSEs, the Purchase Preference Policy must
continue. It may be extended beyond 31
st April, 2002 at least for two more years.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS AT A GLANCE
           
The Committee is of the opinion that the work relating to retraining and redeployment of rationalised employees of central PSEs recently assigned
to the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) is an important matter in the present context, which needs to be reviewed and monitored periodically.
( 2.5)
 
The Committee feels that autonomy of  PSUs should not be limited by Govt. control and such Companies should be fully Board-managed
Companies in all matters. In an environment of stiff competition in the post liberalisation era, the PSUs can not function effectively without
sufficient freedom of operation and level playing field. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Boards of Directors of at least MOU-signing
Companies should be given sufficient powers to enable them to take quick decisions in their business related  matters, by reviewing the extent of the
current powers relating to limit on investment, access to capital market, repayment of foreign loans, foreign visits  by Boards of Directors for their
business position,  forming of joint ventures, exploring foreign markets etc. 
 
            The Committee feels that many PSUs remain headless without any CMD for a long time. This cripples the functioning of the PSUs.
Therefore, as and when any PSU is without CMD for three months, immediate action should be taken to appoint CMD. The Committee understands
that the appointments of CMDs of Central  PSUs is done by Public Enterprises Selection Board. Earlier this Board was under the Department of
Public Enterprises which is presently being controlled by the Ministry of Personnel & Training . The Committee, therefore,  recommends that this
Board may be shifted from the purview of  the Ministry of Personnel Training  to the Department of Public Enterprises for an effective monitoring
of  the functioning of the Central PSUs.

           CHAPTER I
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
 
 
 
ROLE OF MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND AGRO &
RURAL INDUSTRIES IN THE POST LIBERALISATION ERA
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            Ministry’s role at this juncture becomes of paramount importance as it has to evolve mechanisms/directives/guidelines,
which will go a long way in shaping the course of things in future.  In view of these threats, safeguarding the interests of
indigenous industry is the major responsibility of the Ministry while formulating policies.  Government should provide level
playing field for the small scale industry to meet the challenges of stiff competition from global players.
 
COMMENTS
 
            To strengthen the small scale sector and  enhance its competitiveness, both domestically and globally, a comprehensive
policy package was announced on 30
th August, 2000 which inter-alia includes enhancement of excise exemption limit to Rs.1
crore, credit linked capital subsidy of 12% for technology up gradation, increase in investment limit in respect of industry related
service and business enterprises to Rs.10 lakh, enhancement of limit of collateral free composite loans from Rs.10 lakh to Rs.25
lakh, extension of  Integrated Infrastructure Development (IID) scheme to all areas, enhancement of limit of funding under
National Equity Fund Scheme of SIDBI from Rs.25 lakh to Rs. 50 lakh with 30% of the fund   earmarked for tiny sector, the
enhancement in eligibility limit under Credit Guarantee Scheme from Rs.10 lakh to Rs.25 lakh, the ongoing scheme of grant of
Rs.75,000 to each small scale enterprise for obtaining ISO 9000 Certification to be continued till the end of 10
th Plan, assistance of
one time capital grant of 50% on reimbursement basis to SSI associations etc.  
 
            The implementation of this policy package has been a focus area for the Ministry, 29 action points emerged out of this
package - follow up action has been completed in respect of 26 points.  This will go a long way in supporting SSIs.
 
            To enable hi-tech and export oriented industries in small scale sector, to have technology and quality upgradation and to be
able to have level playing field in the international market, Government de-reserved readymade garments.  The de-reservation of
toys and leather goods has also been effected recently.  The draft notification for enhancement of investment limit in respect of
hand tools and knitwears is laid before the Parliament and the final notification is expected shortly.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee has been given to understand that the competitive fervor unleashed by the liberalization process has led to a
paradigm shift in the nature of manufacturing activity in the country.  In such a scenario it has become imperative that the policy of
protection for small-scale sector should pave its way to a more proactive approach of helping such units to enhance their
competitiveness in a market driven economy.  If small and tiny enterprises have to compete in globalised environment they now
require an enabling and responsive environment, which provides adequate and timely credit and pragmatic institutional,
technological and infrastructural support.  The Committee hopes that the above proposals announced in the budget would mitigate
the hardships faced by the SSI Sector. The Government should, however, not feel complacent about this.
 
 
COMMENTS
 
            The Government is keeping constant watch on the changing environment. To ensure effective implementation of the
comprehensive policy package, there is a Policy Implementation Committee under the Chairmanship of AS & DC (SSI) and as
detailed above, action has already been completed in respect of 26 out of 29 points.  The Study Group on Development of Small
Scale Enterprises (Dr. S.P. Gupta Committee) has also submitted its final report, recommendations of which are under final
consideration of the Government.  The Working Group on SSI for the Tenth Plan is also looking into these issues particularly,
credit, technology, marketing and infrastructural support which could be provided to this sector.

REDUCTION OF PLAN OUTLAY AT R.E. STAGE
 
RECOMMENDATIONS
 
            The Committee recommends that the Ministry should visualize the pros and cons of schemes before earmarking
funds.  Allocation of funds should be made depending on feasibility of scheme only.
 
 
COMMENTS
 
            This is correlated to Para 2.3, which pertains to the concern of the Committee regarding reduction in plan outlay at RE
stage. In this connection it is pertinent to note that BE and RE were same for SIDO for the year 2000-2001.However committee’s
observation has been noted.  The Working Group on Tenth Plan is also engaged in the task of recommending appropriate schemes
for the SSI Sector after taking into account the changed domestic and global scenario and also the targeted growth rate.
 
 
 
OFFICE OF DEVELOPMENT COMMISSIONER FOR
SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES
 
RECOMMENDATIONS
 
            The Office of DC (SSI) which is also known as Small Industries Development Organisation is an apex body of the Ministry
and its role has increased to a great extent after the lifting of quantitative restrictions.  The Committee feels that the office of DC
should help the Small Scale Sector in evolving marketing strategies.  To help SSI sector, it should have well equipped computer
network for dissemination of information to that sector.  Technological upgradation is another area where its help to Small Scale
Sector is needed most and the office of DC should play a key role in improving the quality of the products of the SSI sector. 
Therefore, the office of DC needs to be further strengthened and, if necessary, its present allocation may be revised.
 
COMMENTS
 
            In order to strengthen the Office of DC (SSI), its Plan outlay has been enhanced from Rs. 266.50 crore in 1999-2000 to Rs.
379.55 crore in 2000-01 and further to Rs. 390.44 crore in 2001-2002. The Office has taken measures to enable the SSI Sector to
face the challenges after the removal of Quantitative Restrictions. Steps taken for providing market support include formulation of
SSI Exporters Market Development Assistance (SSI – MDA) Scheme to encourage the efforts of SSI Exporters in tapping and
developing overseas markets, organising Vendor Development Programmes–cum–Buyer–Seller–Meets and Exhibitions at different
locations all over the country, conducting Training  Programmes on Packaging for exports to acquaint SSI exporters with the latest
packaging techniques/standards, reservation of 358 items exclusively for purchases from Small Scale Sector under the Government
Stores Purchase Programme and  constitution of a sub-group on marketing and export for SSI Sector under the Chairmanship of
CMD, NSIC.
 
For Technology upgradation the following measures have been taken up:
 
Ø
      A Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme for Technology Upgradation was operationalised with effect from  1st
October, 2000  wherein 12% back ended Capital Subsidy is admissible on loans advanced  to small scale industries by
the scheduled commercial banks/designated SFCs for technology upgradation in select products/sub-products of known 
proven technologies.
 
Ø
      The office of DC(SSI) has introduced an incentive scheme of ISO-9000 certification, which aims at encouraging
technology upgradation and quality improvement in the SSI Sector and preparing it to face the global competition. The
scheme provides reimbursement of 70% of the amount spent for acquiring ISO 9000 certification(or its equivalent) upto
Rs. 75,000 to each SSI Unit. The Scheme has been in operation since March,1994 and 1384 cases have been reimbursed
upto 31.3.2001.The government has extented the scheme till the end of the 10
th Five Year Plan. The office of DC(SSI)
has simultaneously taken up Awareness & Motivational Programme on ISO 9000 and TQM Quality Systems.
 
Ø      Setting up of Incubation Centres in Sunrise Industries-The Secretaries of Ministries/Departments dealing with  Sunrise
Industries have been requested to consider the setting up of Incubation Centres in their respective areas. A Budget
provision of Rs.10 lakh has also been kept for the financial year 2001-2002 to provide the assistance, if required, by
them.

SIDBI and NSIC.  NSIC’s compendium has been hosted on NSIC’s Web site.   SIDBI has recently prepared a

.

Moreover, to address the computerisation related needs of SIDO, a project called Small Enterprises Information & Resource
Centre Network (SENET) was started on Ist April, 1997. The project was revised in March, 2000 to include office automation and
web enabled applications with a total project cost of Rs.1140.38 lakh.  It functions with 5 Technology Nodal Centres and 15 User
Centres, spread all over the country.
 
The Prime objective of SENET is to facilitate the networking amongst the information providers and seekers (National /
State level Industries Associations, NGOs and the entrepreneurs) as well as Central/ State Governments, other Central/ State
agencies engaged directly or indirectly in the promotion and development of the small scale sector.  The data base created by
SENET regarding investment opportunities in the country etc. will be put on world wide web (Internet) to facilitate global access
and making the website accessible by the entrepreneurs 24 hours (round the clock).
 
Further, the Ministry has recently launched its portal on SSI, which not only gives updated online information on
policies/programmes of the Ministry, but also provides links to other related web-sites.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
4.4
 
NATIONAL SMALL INDUSTRIES CORPORATION
 
RECOMMENDATIONS
            The  Committee observes that the Government is not providing financial assistance to the NSIC in the form of equity. 
NSIC is projected to generate Rs. 120.00 crore in budget 2000-01.  Devoid of equity support, NSIC would be hard pressed to
generate revenue on its own now.  The Committee therefore recommends that NSIC should take measures to increase IEBR and
explore ways and means for more revenue generation to become self sufficient.  Till NSIC becomes self reliant, the govt. may
continue to provide funds for the Corporation so that its development activities continue unabated.   
COMMENTS
 
            The Government continues to provide funds for the development activities. For the year 2001-2002, a plan budget of Rs. 29
crore has been provided to NSIC for Marketing Assistance, Development  of N.E. regions, Modernisation  programme, Exchange
variation losses and reimbursement of expenditure of NTSCs and Govt. purchases. A provision of Rs. 5.5 crore (Non Plan) has also
been made for NSIC for reimbursement of expenditure & Govt. purchases to NTSC Okhla, NTSC Rajkot and  NTSC Howrah.
            The Government had approved IEBR of Rs. 517.00 crore for the Corporation during the 9
th Plan period. During the first
four years of the 9th Plan period i.e. during 1997-98 to 2000-01, an amount of Rs. 478.91 crore has been raised by the Corporation
out of Rs. 517.00 crore proposed for the Ninth Five Year Plan.  Further NSIC has been given IEBR mobilisation target of Rs. 120
crore for 2000-2001. The NSIC has already been provided with an equity support of Rs. 58 crores during the Ninth Plan. Action on
enhancing the Equity support will be taken after considering the report of the Consultant appointed for the restructuring of the
NSIC.
 
 
OTHER SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES SCHEMES

RECOMMENDATIONS
           
The Committee hopes that the schemes viz. Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Technology Upgradation, Integrated
Infrastructural Development Scheme, Technology Upgradation and collection of statistics etc. would be implemented successfully
and the targets fixed-both physical and financial would be achieved.  In view of lifting of Quantitative Restrictions, the time has
come to lay more emphasis on technological upgradation and modernisation.  For this purpose, if need be, allocation may be
increased.
 
COMMENTS
 
            The Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme has been recently operationalized by SIDBI (Nodal Agency) through scheduled
commercial banks/NSIC and an advance of Rs. 5.00 Crore has already been given to SIDBI last year. An outlay of Rs. 25 crore
exists for the current year. The progress of scheme would be closely monitored.  At present the scheme covers only 14 sub sectors
of SSI sector.  The scope and coverage of the scheme can be expanded by including more sub-sectors on the advice of Governing
Technology Advisory Board (GTAB) along with the enhancement of Budget provisions accordingly. 
 
            Under the UPTECH Scheme, 9 clusters of industries have been taken up for Modernisation and Technology Upgradation. In
addition, 2 National Programmes in collaboration with UNIDO have also been taken up. Funds allocated in RE for 2000-2001 for
UPTECH Scheme were stepped up considerably to give more emphasis on technology upgradation.
 
            The Integrated Infrastructure Development (IID) Scheme earlier covered backward districts/rural areas which were not
covered under the Growth Centres Scheme, being implemented by the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion. The scope
of the scheme has now been extended by covering  all areas in the country.
 
Under the modified scheme  50 percent reservation has been provided for the rural areas and    the funds available  under
the non-lapsable  pool for the North East will be made use  of  for Industrial Infrastructure Development, setting up of incubation
centres, for cluster development and for setting up of IIDs in the North East including Sikkim.
 
Various components of the Plan Scheme “ Collection of Statistics  of SSI “ are progressing as per the targets. The monthly
data for Index of Industrial Production (IIP) are being collected, compiled and supplied to CSO every month. IIP for the SSI Sector
is being compiled every quarter as per the targets. Registration data received from every State/UT Directorate is being compiled
every quarter and data on commulative number of SSI units registered with the State Directorate of Industries (SDIs) are being

ANTI-DUMPING DUTY
RECOMMENDATIONS
 
            The Committee observes that it takes 90 days to review economic fallout of imported goods in country and imposition of
anti-dumping duties thereon.  By that time huge financial losses would have already occurred to the country, which are
irretrievable.  The Committee observes that in order to preclude the possibility of economic losses, anti-dumping monitoring should
be expedited.  The Committee therefore recommends that the administrative ministry should review the pros and cons in this regard
and take timely action.  The system that exists in other countries may be examined.  India can also emulate such a system.
 
COMMENTS
The Anti-Dumping Authority in the Ministry of Commerce & Industry is fully geared up to decide any formal complaints of
dumping by any country expeditiously.  In view of the legitimate demand of the domestic industry to provide immediate relief in
the face of dumping faced by them, the Directorate General of Anti-dumping & Allied Duties (DGAD), has streamlined its process
of investigation and Preliminary Findings are now being issued within a period of two-and-a-half to three months from the date of
initiation as against over six months being taken in the previous years.
The DGAD also actively participated in the workshops/seminars in different parts of the country organized by Association
of Industries to disseminate information on anti-dumping laws and procedures and to facilitate the domestic industry in submitting
their properly documented petitions for initiation of cases. India is one of the leading users of Anti-Dumping  measures in the
world. As Per the WTO report of 2000 India was the most active member during the year 1999 in terms of initiation of Anti-
Dumping investigations followed by EU, USA, and Argentina. At the same time, the transparency and thoroughness of our
investigations is borne out by the fact that not a single case initiated by DGAD has been brought before the Dispute Settlement
Body by any of the exporting countries.  We have been using the anti-dumping mechanisms very effectively.
The Directorate takes approximately 3 months to bring the preliminary findings of an Anti-dumping initiation.  In terms of
time taken for issue of preliminary findings, India compares favourably with other important users of Anti-Dumping measures in
the world.
 
Country Average Time Taken
India Approx.3 months
USA Approx.4-5 months
EU Approx.7-8months
Australia Approx. 5 months
New Zealand Approx.5-6 months
 
 
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS
 
            The Committee understands that enacting law in this matter is not the concern of this ministry.  The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the matter may be taken up with the concerned administrative ministry for making a law, if necessary.  Otherwise
necessary regulations may be prepared by the concerned Ministry and the Ministry of Small Scale Industries & Agro and Rural
Industries may pursue it.
 
COMMENTS

63rd Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/63rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:13:33]
The matter was taken up with Directorate General of Anti-dumping & Allied Duties(DGAD), Ministry of Commerce &
Industry, who have informed that the Designated Authority appointed by the Government conducts Anti-Dumping investigations in
India under Sections 9A, 9B and 9C of the Customs Tariff Act of 1975 as amended in 1995. According to the Anti-Dumping Rules
the initiation of Anti-Dumping investigations is undertaken when the domestic industry files a fully documented petition to the
Designated Authority with prima-facie evidence of dumping, injury and causal link between the dumping of the imported goods
and injury to the domestic industry. However, under the rule 5(4) of  the Customs Tariff Rules of 1995, the Designated Authority
may  initiate investigations suo-moto if it is satisfied with the information recevied from the Collector of Customs appointed under
the Customs Act, 1962 or from any other source that sufficient evidence exists regarding dumping of the foreign goods, material
injury to the domestic industry and causal link between the two.
Article VI of WTO Agreements prescribes the guidelines on Anti-Dumping measures to be followed by the member
countries for imposition of anti-dumping duties and countervailing duties. The guidelines are designed on the previous anti-
dumping code under Article VI of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and states as to how the member countries
can invoke anti-dumping duties against another member country. The new guidelines inter-alia provide time limits for various
stages of investigations to be conducted, the methodology of determination of the extent of anti-dumping and the measures to be
adopted by the member countries.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS
 
            The Committee feels that availability of imported commodities, relatively of cheap quality without carrying MRP and ISI
labels, poses a serious threat to the domestic industries, particularly the small scale sector.  The Government should look into this
matter on priority basis and take all appropriate measures to protect the interests of domestic industries from unfair competition
from imported goods.
 
COMMENTS
 
The Government is closely monitoring the imports and all necessary steps to safeguard the interests of the domestic industry
are being taken. A Notification has been issued by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry on 24.11.2000, regarding compliance of
all the conditions of the Standards of Weights and Measures (packaged commodity) Order, 1977, on imports as applicable to
domestic producers.  In addition, the importers of packaged commodities have to comply with the following conditions:
 
a)
      Name and address of the importer,
b)      Generic or common name of the commodity packed;
c)      Net quantity in terms of standard units of weights and measures, if the net quantity in the imported package is given to
any other unit, its equivalent in terms of standard units shall be declared by the importer;
d)      Month and year of packing in which the commodity is manufactured or packed or imported;
e)      Maximum retail sale  price (MRP) at which the commodity in packaged form may be sold to the ultimate consumer. 
This price shall include all taxes, local or otherwise, freight transport charges, commission payable to dealers and all
charges towards advertising, delivery, packing, forwarding and the like as the case may be.
 
The Notification also makes the import of 131 products subject to compliance with  the mandatory India quality standards
as applicable to  domestic goods.  For compliance of this requirement all manufacturers/ exporters of these products to India shall
be required to register themselves with the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).  The list of 131 products includes various food
preservatives and additives, milk powder, infant milk food, certain kinds of cement, household and similar electrical appliances and
multi-purpose dry batteries.

RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee recommends that efforts should be made to bridge the gap between the sanctioned cases and actual
disbursal of loans under PMRY.  The Committee also recommends that the number of beneficiaries should be increased.  If
necessary, allocation may be increased at RE stage.
 
COMMENTS
 
As per the report received from the RBI, loans were sanctioned to 7,91,850 persons during the years 1997-98; 1998-99 and
1999-2000.  During the year 2000-01 loans were sanctioned to 2,29,437 persons and disbursed to 1,27,890 persons against the
target of 2,20,000 as reported by the RBI.  The figure for disbursement is likely to go up as the cut off date for completion of
disbursement has been stipulated as 31.12.2001.
 
            However, the RBI has been requested to issue necessary instructions to the implementing banks to speed up the process of
disbursement to bridge the gap between sanctions and disbursements.  The State/UTs have also been requested to arrange training
and other pre-disbursal formalities so that the gap between the sanctions and disbursement is reduced. 
 
            To ensure the achievement of plan target of 2,20,000 at national level, better performing States are allocated additional
target in addition to basic targets.  However, some States/UTs could not achieve the basic target due to various socio-economic
factors e.g. militancy and unstable political situation and due to reluctance on the part of banks to disburse loan on account of poor
recovery of loan overdues.  However, the RBI as well as the States/UTs have been requested to achieve the allocated target and
bridge the gap between sanctions and disbursement. 
 
Over and above the plan target of 2.20 lakh for 2001-2002 an additional target of 1.07 lakh have been allocated to better
performing States/UTs.  Due to the requirement of undergoing training and completion of pre-disbursement formalities, the loan for
the cases sanctioned in the year 2001-2002 may also be disbursed in 2002-2003. Depending upon the requirement of funds, the
Budget Estimate for 2002-2003 will be worked out.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
 
The Committee feels that there is a need to keep a constant vigil over the loan disbursement under  PMRY particularly on
the non-target achieving states. Before allocating  fresh target it should be ensured that the earlier target has been achieved.

disbursed and rejected with reasons therefor for the year 2001-2002.

RECOMMENDATIONS
 
 
            The Committee recommends that the policy package for credit guarantee scheme may be made operational at the earliest in
case it has not been made as yet.  The Committee also feels that the lengthy bureaucratic red tapism in clearing credit needs to be
removed and rules be simplified and made easy.
 
COMMENTS
 
            Credit Guarantee Scheme has been launched in August, 2000 to provide guarantee for loans upto Rs.25 lakh  extended by
the commercial banks, selected well performing Regional Rural Banks and other Financial Institutions  without any collateral 
including third party guarantee.  A Credit Guarantee Fund Trust of SIDBI (CGTSI) has been created to implement the Scheme.   18
Scheduled Commercial Bank, 1 Regional Rural Bank, National Small Industries Corporation and North Eastern Development
Finance Corporation have registered with CGTSI as Member Lending Institutions for availing guarantee facility. Upto July, 2001, 
2009 cases have been sanctioned with guarantee cover extended for an aggregate credit of Rs. 12.86 crore.
 
            The application forms for loans have been  simplified based on the recommendations of the Nayak Committee.
Computation of credit needs has also been made simple by computing it on the basis of 20% of the projected annual turnover upto a
borrowal limit of Rs.5 crore. As per the extant guidelines, application for credit limits up to Rs. 25000, is to be disposed of within a
fortnight and those for loans beyond Rs.25000 within 8 to 9 weeks. The recommendation of Study Group on Development of Small
Scale Enterprises (Dr S.P.Gupta Committee) that loan applications up to Rs 5 Lakh may be disposed within a month, is under
consideration.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS
 
            The Committee feels that the  S.P. Gupta  Committee recommendation on fast processing of loan applications be  dealt on a
priority  basis and an early decision be taken.

availing guarantee facility. The Committee recommends that SIDBI should ensure that all the Public Sector banks should register
with it for the purpose.

            The Committee recommends that the tax – exempt status as provided in the Small Industries Development Bank of India

             The matter has been taken up with the Ministry of Finance to restore the tax-exempt status of SIDBI as before. In their
reply, Ministry of Finance has mentioned that a conscious policy decision was taken to remove Section 50 of SIDBI Act which
pertains to income tax exemption available to SIDBI. This decision has been taken in view of the fact that the institution is in
existence for a  considerable period now and has been working on commercial basis, therefore, there is no rationale for retaining
tax exemption while similar institutions are paying their taxes.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS
 
The Committee understands that the concessional resource support available to SIDBI            in earlier years from
Government of India/RBI have gradually depleted. By this, SIDBI has been forced to approach open market for mobilizing
resource requirements. The Committee has also been given to understand that expectations from various quarters for investment by

INDO-NEPAL TRADE TREATY
 
RECOMMENDATIONS
 
The Committee would like the Ministry to look into this aspect of unfair competition being posed by the imports from
Nepal. The Committee understands that the Indo-Nepal Trade Treaty is due for review during the later part of 2001. It would,
therefore, recommend that this matter may be looked into and corrective measures taken.
 
COMMENTS
 
            Import from Nepal is governed by the  Indo-Nepal Treaty on Trade and Transit. The Indo-Nepal Treaty was last amended in
December, 1996 and is valid upto 5
th December, 2001. The Treaty will be automatically renewed in the normal course if either side
gives no notice. During the last amendment in December, 1996, the existing value addition norms were deleted and all products
manufactured in Nepal were eligible for duty free exports to India.  In the absence of value addition norms there has been a rapid
growth of imports into India of some Nepalese commodities. This has led to representations from domestic industries in these
sectors. Representations have been received regarding excessive import of many products. The industry has pointed out that in
absence of proper  rules of origin, Nepal has become a re-export point for many of the products from China and other South Asian
countries. The provision of certificate of origin was dispensed with in the new treaty. This has given rise to a spurt in flow of
Chinese goods in the guise of Nepalese goods which has badly affected the Indian industry particularly small scale and medium
industry as they are unable to compete with the cheap Chinese goods which are coming via Nepal.
 
            The Indo-Nepal Treaty is due for review shortly and these concerns can be addressed at the time of review. In the best
interest of Indian Trade and Industry it is essential now to review the Indo-Nepal Treaty, making it mandatory for goods
manufactured in Nepal to be accompanied by the certificate of origin and prescribing value addition norms. Nepal's accession to
WTO is also to be negotiated shortly and these issues of Indian concerns can also be taken up at that time.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee hopes that the anomalies arising out of Indo-Nepal treaty in the new scenario would be addressed to and
concrete measures would be taken to redress the grievances of Indian manufacturers at the time of review of the treaty.

REPORT
 
            The Offshore Areas Mineral (Development And Regulation) Bill, 2001 was referred to the Committee on
Industry by the Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha on  7
th September, 2001 under  Rule 270(b) of the Rules of Procedure
and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha for examination and report thereon.
2          The Bill aims to provide for development and regulation of mineral resources in the territorial  waters,
continental shelf, exclusive economic zone and other maritime zones of India and   to provide  for matters connected
therewith or incidental  thereto.
3          According to   the statement of objects and reasons of the Bill, the need was felt to have  proper legal   frame
work for   regulation and  development of minerals occurring  in the offshore areas, that is,  territorial waters,
continental shelf, exclusive  economic zone and other maritime zones of  India, in order to develop the offshore  areas
scientifically and  systematically.   India  has approximately 3.3 million square kilometres  of land area  with a coast line
of 8041 kilometres. The area of the Exclusive Economic Zone is 2.02 million square kilometres and  in terms of the UN
Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982,  the coastal states have specific rights and jurisdiction, inter alia,  for exploring
and exploiting the natural resources over the continental margin, which will add about 0.80 million square kilometres in
addition to the area of Exclusive Economic Zone. In  India, beach placer deposits have been economically exploited
since long. The mining and processing of different minerals obtained from these placer deposits into valuable products

are also well established. India is richly endowed in mineral sands in the Eastern and Western Coasts. Heavy mineral
sand containing mostly  ilmenite with some rutile, leucoxene (a decomposition product of ilmenite), garnet, zircon,
monazite and aluminium silicates like silimanite and kyanite occur in isolated to extensive spreads all along the sea
coast.
4          The proposed legislation would enable streamlining of mineral exploration and development in the offshore
areas and ensure systematic and scientific exploitation of mineral reserves (except petroleum, natural gas and
hydrocarbon resources) for attracting private investment in the mineral sector.
5.         Under the Law of the Sea  convention, 1982, the coastal states   are  entitled to territorial sea (12 nautical miles), 
contiguous zone (24 nautical miles) exclusive  economic zone (200 nautical miles) and   continental shelf (200/350
nautical  miles) drawn from normal base-line, which is the low-water line along  the coast,  over which the  coastal
States have specific rights and Jurisdiction, including for  exploring and  exploiting the natural  resources.  The
Convention   came into effect  on 16
th November, 1994 and became part of the  International Law, India has ratified the
Law of the Sea Convention on  29th June, 1995.  Article  297 of the Constitution of India was amended by the  40th
Amendment to the Constitution and according to amended Article 297 , all lands , minerals and other things of value
underlying the  ocean within the   territorial water, or the continental shelf, or the exclusive economic zone of  India, 
shall vest in the Union and be held for the purposes  of the Union.  In 1976, the Parliament passed the Territorial
Waters, Continental Shelf , Exclusive  Economic zone and other Maritime Zones Bill, 1976 delineating therein the
limits of the zones and rights and obligations in maritime zones.
6.         Entry  54 of   List-I of the Constitution gives powers to the Central Government for regulation of mines and
mineral development to the extent to which such regulation and  development under the control of the   Union is
declared by  Parliament by law to be  expedient in the public interest.  The Bill has been introduced accordingly. 
Further, the  clauses 16 and 17 of the Bill provide that royalty and fixed rent shall be payable to the Central Government
and, therefore, in accordance with Article 117 (1) of the  Constitution of India, which requires  that any Bill making
provision for any of the matters specified in sub-clauses (a) to (f)   of clause (1)  of article110   [Definition of   "Money
Bills."] ,  recommendation of the President has been obtained prior to introduction of the Bill.
7.         As per amendments  made  on November, 10, 1992 to the  Allocation of  Business Rules,  1961, legislation for
regulation  of mines and development of minerals underlying  the ocean within the territorial waters, or the continental 
shelf of the exclusive   economic zone and other maritime   zones of India has been placed under the charge of the
Department of Mines.  In May,.  1993 a working group was constituted, headed  by the Joint Secretary, Department of
Mines, for finalising the legislation for offshore areas .  Terms of reference of the working group were  (i) to suggest a
suitable legislation and rules for regulating prospecting and mining in the  Territorial Waters, c Continental Shelf and
Exclusive Economic Zone of India after examining the existing legislation of the  subject viz.  the Mines and Minerals
(Development and Regulation) Act, 1957  (MMDR Act) , and the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive
Economic Zone and other Maritime Zone Act, 1976 and other related matters; and (ii) to make any  other
recommendations as may be considered necessary.  The working group    has taken into consideration the opinion
expressed  by Ministry of Law, ( January, 1974) that if, by virtue of special requirement of minerals in the offshore
areas, it is considered necessary to lay down conditions or restriction which are at variance with the existing statutory
provisions in the MMDR Act, 1957 , then under such circumstances, it would not be legally permissible to do  so
without first   amending the statute, i.e. MMDR Act, 1957  itself suitably.  It was  also observed that by virtue of Article
297 of the Constitution, the ownership of minerals in the offshore areas vests  in the Union and if the MMDR Act were
to be used for  framing rules applicable to offshore areas  it would require extensive amendments.   The Wording Group
also  examined the possibility of framing Rules under section 15 of the Maritime Zone act, 1976.  It was observed 
however, that the Maritime Zones  Act   is in the nature of umbrella legislation and if Rules are to be framed under this
Act, provisions normally included  in the Act will   have to  be  necessarily provided for in the Rules,   This  could be a
doubtful course of action, as it would amount to "excessive delegation"  through the rules which is not desirable in  any 
legislation.  The Working  Group, therefore, came to the conclusion that it would be advisable to frame a new Act for
mineral exploitation in offshore areas and submitted its report and draft of the proposed legislation accordingly in
December, 1995.   The Report and the proposed draft legislation was further examined in  extensive consultation with
all Departments and Ministries in the Government of India who have  stakes in off shore areas.  Accordingly the Bill has
been prepared, duly addressing the concerns of all stake holders.
8.         The Bill consists of   38 clauses spreading over six chapters  and two schedules .  Chapter-I of the proposed
legislation, i.e. Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Bill consists of first   4 Clauses of the Bill giving
details of  short title and commencement, Declaration  as to  expediency of Union control, Application, Definitions.

8.1       Clause-1 of the chapter -I gives preliminary information such  as : short title, extent and commencement, Clause-
2   contains   declaration as to expediency of Union to take under its control the regulation of the mines and
development of minerals in offshore areas to enable Parliament to enact the proposed legislation.   Clauses-3 species 
that the proposed legislation shall apply to all minerals in offshore areas except mineral oils and hydrocarbons and the
provisions of the  proposed legislation shall be in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the  time being
in  force in the offshore areas.  This would  ensure that the strategic and defence  interests of the country are fully
safeguarded.   Clause -4   contains  the definitions in the proposed legislation, which, inter-alia, includes definitions like 
`administering authority', `exploration licence,   `exploration operations',  `mine',   `off shore areas',  `pollution of
offshore environment', `production lease', reconnaissance operation', reconnaissance permit etc. In the proposed
legislation  there would be three types of operating rights,  namely reconnaissance permit (non exclusive), exploration
licence and production lease. Clause 4 (v)  states that  reconnaissance permit means a permit granted under section 11
for the purpose of undertaking reconnaissance operation.  While  the production  lease means   a lease granted  under
section 13 which confers an exclusive right for the purpose of undertaking production operation.   Production operation
means any operation undertaken for the purpose of winning any mineral from the offshore area and includes any
operation directly or indirectly necessary therefor or incidental thereto.  Clause 4 (u) states reconnaissance operation
means any  preliminary geo-scientific  survey undertaken for the purpose of searching or locating mineral deposits.
8.2.      Chapter-II deals with  General Provisions for Acquisition of  Operating Rights in the Offshore Areas.  Clause 5,
provides that no person shall undertake any reconnaissance operation,  exploration operation or production   operation 
in the  offshore areas except under and in accordance  with the prescribed terms and conditions of the  reconnaissance 
permit,  exploration licence  or production lease granted under  the proposed legislation and the rules made thereunder. 
The clause also enables agencies of the  Central Government  including the  Geological Survey of India, Atomic
Mineral Directorate of Exploration and Research, Naval Hydrographic office, National Institute of  oceanography and
the  National Institute  of  Ocean Technology to carry out  reconnaissance  and  exploration operations without requiring
a permit or license  under the proposed  legislation.  This clause lays down the various requirements  regarding
dissemination of the data generated which the  permitee or licensee  or a lessee has to furnish   and also seeks to
empower the  Central Government to provide for  special measures as may be required for seaward artillery practice  ,
ensuring public safety and interest, defence of India and civil defence , conduct of naval operations and exercises,
national   security and other strategic  considerations.  This clause further ensures that scientific research carried out by
the Central Government  agencies is not fettered by the proposed legislation.
